name: The Breakers Palm Beach
insider_take: This legendary oceanfront palace has been the crown jewel of Palm Beach since 1896, where Gilded Age grandeur meets modern luxury on 140 pristine acres.
whats_special: The Breakers is built in the style of an Italian Renaissance palace and features hand-painted ceilings, imported marble, and crystal chandeliers throughout. The resort boasts Florida's oldest golf course (1897) and sits on 1,200 feet of private Atlantic coastline. Its iconic Flagler Steakhouse occupies the original hotel's site, while the property's main building survived multiple reconstructions to become a National Historic Landmark.
pro_tip: Book afternoon tea at The Tapestry Bar during winter season (December-April) when Palm Beach's social scene is at its peak—you'll spot seasonal residents and catch glimpses of old Florida high society.
dont_miss: A stroll down Worth Avenue, America's answer to Rodeo Drive, located just steps from the hotel. Also explore the Henry Morrison Flagler Museum (Whitehall), the stunning Gilded Age mansion turned museum that showcases the vision of The Breakers' original founder.
pros: Iconic oceanfront location with pristine private beach access
Historic luxury resort with timeless elegance and grandeur
Multiple award-winning dining venues and world-class spa facilities
Extensive recreational amenities including golf course and tennis courts
cons: Large resort size may feel less intimate for some guests
